name: Subacoustic Vestibular Collapse Drone SVCD-1 'Tilt'
description:
The SVCD-1 is a compact, agile drone platform built around a single, highly specialized function: the generation of precisely calibrated subacoustic waveforms tuned to the resonant frequencies of the human vestibular system. Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION's non-lethal compliance division, the drone produces infrasound pulses in the 0.5–4 Hz range directed through a focused parabolic emitter array at its ventral surface. When these waveforms intersect with a target's inner ear structures, they induce a rapid and total loss of spatial orientation — targets cannot determine up from down, cannot maintain balance, and experience severe nausea within seconds of sustained exposure.

The SVCD-1's engineering challenge was directionality: infrasound at these frequencies is notoriously difficult to focus, and early prototypes affected entire rooms rather than individual targets. TESSERA's solution was a multi-emitter phased array system that uses destructive interference to cancel the waveform outside a narrow 15-degree cone, concentrating the full effect on a single target while leaving adjacent individuals largely unaffected. The system requires continuous tracking to maintain this cone alignment, which is handled by the drone's onboard inertial targeting processor — a TESSERA proprietary unit derived from their precision manufacturing alignment systems.

Beyond immediate incapacitation, repeated or prolonged exposure has been documented to cause lasting vestibular sensitization, where affected individuals experience spontaneous vertigo episodes for weeks afterward when exposed to ordinary low-frequency vibration — engines, heavy machinery, certain music. This residual effect is not listed in TESSERA's official product documentation.
specifications:
dimensions: 24cm x 20cm x 8cm
infrasound frequency range: 0.5–4 Hz
emission cone angle: 15 degrees
effective range: 4m–20m
time to incapacitation: 3–8 seconds sustained exposure
targeting system: TESSERA inertial precision tracking processor
power source: High-output polymer capacitor array
battery life: 35 minutes continuous operation
weight: 1.6kg
documented residual effect: Vestibular sensitization, duration 1–4 weeks post-exposure
tactical_use: The SVCD-1 is used primarily to neutralize high-mobility targets — runners, combat-augmented individuals, anyone whose primary defensive asset is speed and agility. A target that cannot stand cannot run. Operators typically deploy the SVCD-1 ahead of a ground team's advance, using the drone to drop a target in place for easy approach and restraint. It is also used in vertical environments — stairwells, scaffolding, elevated platforms — where induced loss of balance carries additional fall hazard. Security teams protecting fixed positions use it as a perimeter drone, set to intercept approach vectors and trigger on any confirmed human signature.
cultural_context: The SVCD-1 is one of the few drone weapons in common circulation that its manufacturer actively markets by name in public-facing security trade publications, positioning it as a 'precision human compliance instrument.' This visibility has made it a symbol of TESSERA CORPONATION's aggressive normalization of non-lethal weaponry in civilian security contexts. The undocumented residual sensitization effect has become a source of legal action from several advocacy groups, with plaintiffs describing a life altered by vertigo they cannot explain — a condition colloquially called 'Tilt sickness' in affected communities.
known_users: Private residential tower security teams (upper district)
Freelance crowd management operators with Tier 3 licensing
story_hooks: A support group for 'Tilt sickness' sufferers has started quietly collecting evidence of undocumented SVCD-1 residual effects — and their meeting space has just been broken into, with all their records taken.

The players need to cross a TESSERA-secured facility whose SVCD-1 perimeter drones are networked to a central inertial processor — if they can spoof one drone's tracking data, the entire perimeter may be compromised.

A former TESSERA compliance division engineer is auctioning off documentation proving the residual sensitization effect was known before the SVCD-1 went to market — the bidders include journalists, lawyers, and at least one corporate cleanup crew.

physical_description.visual_profile: A low-slung, almost predatory disc with a slightly convex upper hull and a broader, flatter ventral surface. Four articulated arms radiate outward from the central body, each tipped with stabilizing rotors that seem almost delicate against the weapon's purposeful geometry. The overall impression is of something designed to hang in space and *listen* — sleek, precise, deliberately minimal.
physical_description.dimensions: 24cm diameter, 20cm depth (rotor to rotor), 8cm height (hull to hull)
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light in hand — 1.6kg — which creates an unsettling contrast with its operational density. Feels like expensive, engineered precision rather than brute force.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite hull with aerospace-grade aluminum spine. The ventral emitter array is a precision-machined polymer matrix embedded with phased ceramic transducers.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite with brushed aluminum accent panels around the emitter array. Heat dissipation grilles etched in geometric patterns. Industrial, medical-grade precision rather than tactical aesthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte dark gray primary hull with silver-gray aluminum trim. The exposed phased-array emitters catch light like a circuit board — faint iridescence in certain angles revealing the ceramic matrix beneath.
physical_description.grip_texture: The rotor arms feature thin rubberized contact points; the central hub has minimal grip texture — this is a drone designed to be cradled, not gripped. When docked, it nests into custom carry frames with tactile polymer locators.
distinctive_features: Four independently articulated rotor arms with synchronized motion control
Ventral phased-array emitter dish — concentric rings of ceramic transducers arranged in a focused parabolic geometry
Subtle LED status indicators along the rotor mounts (green: operational, amber: tracking, red: emission active)
Precision gyroscopic stabilization spines visible along the hull perimeter
TESSERA proprietary inertial targeting processor module — small raised panel on the dorsal surface with circuit-trace detailing
Micro-port array for capacitor exchange and firmware updates
Faint engraving around the central hub reading 'SVCD-1 TILT | TESSERA CORPORATION | NON-LETHAL COMPLIANCE DIVISION'
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA Corporation logo (a prismatic tessellation mark) embossed on the dorsal hull. Serial number plate beneath the rotor arm junction. Compliance certification stamps in white laser-etching around the perimeter. A small Φ symbol marking it as a Tier 3+ asset.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units typically show fine scuffing on the rotor arms from dock contact. The ventral emitter array stays pristine — operators understand that any physical damage to the ceramic transducers compromises directionality. Some units show faint thermal discoloration on the heat dissipation grilles from extended use. Generally well-maintained; operators treat it like precision laboratory equipment rather than field hardware.
